fact: The Communications Authority consultation states that the ICT Sector Policy Guidelines, 2020 (also called National ICT policy guidelines, 2020) direct government agencies to promote and license private investment in carrier-neutral data centres; no adoption date beyond 2020 is given and the document's published date is 2026-09-01.

CIPIT's analysis lists 'the ICT Policy' among Kenya's existing instruments that recognise inclusion but set no AI accessibility standards or enforcement mechanism; the document gives no adoption date, so the published date 2026-07-30 is used.

The draft AI policy lists the National ICT Policy (2019) among the national policy and strategy instruments that provide guidance on digital transformation, as in place; it gives no adoption date beyond the year, and no event date, so the document's published date is used.

The policy states that the 2006 ICT Sector Policy Guidelines were reviewed and updated to a National ICT Policy in 2019, and lists that policy among the laws and policies supporting implementation, as in place (it also lists a 'National ICT Policy, 2020' once).
The Master Plan states the National ICT Policy 2019 was gazetted in 2020, Gazette Notice No. 5472.
The Master Plan states the National ICT Policy of 2019 was published in a special issue of the Kenya Government Gazette, and quotes its vision and mission.

Research ICT Africa lists the National ICT Policy (2019) among the anchors of Kenya's digital policy architecture and describes its content as an existing instrument covering infrastructure, broadcasting, cybersecurity, e-government, data, innovation, human capacity and emerging technologies.

Research ICT Africa cites the National ICT Policy 2019 to a page on the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy website (ict.go.ke/node/502); no date for the link is given, so the report's September 2026 publication is used.

Research ICT Africa states that the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy has responsibility for policy formulation and overall sector coordination, with the Communications Authority as regulator; no ministry budget line for the ICT policy is stated; dated by the report's September 2026 publication.

The review of the Digital Literacy Programme states that the 2006 National ICT Policy was revised in 2019 and sets objectives for scaling up ICT in education; the review is dated 2022 (no month given).
